The left-footed centre-back provides reliable depth for Bosnia's defensive options and is comfortable on the ball when Rijeka chose to build from the back.
strengths: Championship-winning defensive quality at domestic level
Left-footed centre-back versatility
Strong leadership qualities — named club captain at Rijeka
weaknesses: Limited exposure to top-five European leagues
Aerial duel numbers moderate compared to elite centre-backs

dennis-hadzikadunic.name: Dennis Hadžikadunić
dennis-hadzikadunic.profile: A Swedish-born Bosnian centre-back who spent 2024-25 at Hamburger SV in the 2. Bundesliga, making 25 appearances and scoring 1 goal before joining Sampdoria on loan. An aerial specialist by profile, he brings physical defending and experience across multiple European second-tier competitions. His adaptability and organisational instincts make him a useful squad option for Bosnia.
strengths: Strong in aerial duels
Physical and committed in defensive duels
Versatile — played at various clubs across Europe
weaknesses: Limited success rate in ground duels
Has yet to sustain a spell in a top-five league

nidal-celic.name: Nidal Čelić
nidal-celic.profile: The youngest outfield player in Bosnia's squad, Čelić broke through at FK Sarajevo in 2024-25 — where he was named captain despite his age — before completing a high-profile move to RC Lens in February 2025. At 192cm with exceptional composure, he is viewed as a future cornerstone of Bosnia's defence. His selection for the 2026 World Cup squad at just 19 underscores his enormous potential.
strengths: Exceptional potential and maturity beyond his years
Physical presence and aerial ability at 192cm
Strong passing and ability to play out from the back
weaknesses: Limited Ligue 1 appearances to date
Inexperience at the highest club level yet to be fully tested

amir-hadziahmetovic.name: Amir Hadžiahmetović
amir-hadziahmetovic.profile: A hard-working defensive midfielder who spent 2024-25 primarily on loan at Rizespor in the Süper Lig before returning to Beşiktaş and subsequently moving on loan to Hull City in the Championship. His industry, pressing ability, and reading of the game make him a valued engine room presence for Bosnia's midfield, screening the back four effectively.
strengths: High defensive output and pressing intensity
Excellent positional discipline
Consistent international performer for Bosnia
weaknesses: Limited creative contribution going forward
Has struggled with lack of settled club situation

ivan-sunjic.name: Ivan Šunjić
ivan-sunjic.profile: A physically imposing defensive midfielder who won a first-ever league title with Pafos FC in Cyprus in 2024-25, Šunjić joined the club after leaving Birmingham City and revived his career impressively. His strength, aerial ability, and no-nonsense defending in midfield have kept him in Bosnia's plans despite playing outside the top leagues.
strengths: Physical dominance in midfield battles
Strong aerial ability for a midfielder
Winning mentality — contributed to Pafos title
weaknesses: Disciplinary record limits reliability
Playing standard in Cyprus below top European leagues

ivan-basic.name: Ivan Bašić
ivan-basic.profile: A technically gifted left-footed midfielder who spent 2024-25 at FK Orenburg in the Russian Premier League before joining FC Astana in Kazakhstan, Bašić became the only Kazakhstan Premier League player at the 2026 World Cup after helping Bosnia qualify through the play-offs. His passing accuracy, clever movement, and ability to carry the ball make him a dynamic option from midfield.
strengths: Technical quality and left-footed creativity
Strong passing accuracy under pressure
Composed in tight spaces
weaknesses: Competition standard in Kazakhstan below top European leagues
Physicality in midfield battles still developing

dzenis-burnic.name: Dženis Burnić
dzenis-burnic.profile: A box-to-box midfielder with Dortmund academy roots, Burnić has been a consistent performer for Karlsruher SC in the 2. Bundesliga. His technical ability, pressing and ability to drive through midfield keep him relevant at international level. He is a left-footed central option who provides Bosnia with variety in their midfield configurations.
strengths: Strong technical base from BVB academy
Driving runs from midfield
Consistent 2. Bundesliga performer
weaknesses: Career stagnated outside top-flight football
Disciplinary record can disrupt game plans

ermin-mahmic.name: Ermin Mahmić
ermin-mahmic.profile: One of Bosnia's youngest midfielders, Mahmić spent 2024-25 at SV Lafnitz in Austria's second tier — scoring 4 goals and providing 5 assists in 25 appearances — before signing a four-year contract with Czech First League club Slovan Liberec. An attacking-minded central midfielder with excellent vision and technique, he is a rising talent whose inclusion signals Bosnia's faith in youth.
strengths: Excellent vision and creative passing
Goal contributions from midfield (4G, 5A in 2024-25)
Young with significant ceiling for growth
weaknesses: Experience limited to lower European leagues
Physical development still ongoing

benjamin-tahirovic.name: Benjamin Tahirović
benjamin-tahirovic.profile: A defensive midfielder who came through Roma's academy and had a stint at Ajax before joining Brøndby on a permanent deal in February 2025. His ability to intercept, recycle possession and break up opposition attacks gives Bosnia's midfield a vital screening function. Technical quality honed at top academies makes him one of the squad's higher-potential young profiles.
strengths: Excellent reading of the game
Strong in defensive transitions
Technical quality honed at top academies (Roma, Ajax)
weaknesses: Struggled for regular first-team minutes at Ajax
Scoring output from midfield is limited

amar-memic.name: Amar Memić
amar-memic.profile: A right-sided midfielder who signed for Viktoria Plzeň and featured in their UEFA Europa League campaign, Memić has developed into a reliable attacking-minded option in the Czech top flight. Capable of operating on the right flank or through the middle, he provides Bosnia with a creative midfield option with European competition experience.
strengths: Creativity and forward passing
Europa League experience with Plzeň
Consistent contributions in Czech top flight
weaknesses: Yet to prove himself consistently in a top-five league
Final third decision-making can be inconsistent

armin-gigovic.name: Armin Gigović
armin-gigovic.profile: Gigović had a remarkable 2024-25 Bundesliga season with Holstein Kiel, scoring 5 goals in 31 league appearances — a standout return for a central midfielder in a relegated side. His energy, late runs into the box, and pressing make him one of Bosnia's most dynamic midfield options. He moved to Young Boys for 2025-26 and will use the World Cup as a springboard to a bigger move.
strengths: Strong goal-scoring output from midfield (5 Bundesliga goals)
Dynamic pressing and late runs into the box
Bundesliga-proven quality
weaknesses: Was part of a relegated Bundesliga side in 2024-25
Consistency of passing at the top level can vary

kerim-alajbegovic.name: Kerim Alajbegović
kerim-alajbegovic.profile: The most electrifying teenager in the squad, Alajbegović emerged from Bayer Leverkusen's academy and joined Salzburg for 2025-26, where he scored 7 goals in his debut season. Still only 18, he scored on his senior Bosnia debut and heads to the 2026 World Cup as one of the most exciting young wingers in Eastern Europe. His pace, dribbling, and direct running are weapons Bosnia can deploy from the bench or in wide positions.
strengths: Exceptional pace and direct dribbling
Natural goal threat from the wing (7 goals in debut Salzburg season)
Fearless attitude at the highest level
weaknesses: Limited senior club appearances prior to Salzburg
Consistency and decision-making still raw at 18

esmir-bajraktarevic.name: Esmir Bajraktarević
esmir-bajraktarevic.profile: A MLS homegrown product who completed a $6 million move to PSV Eindhoven in January 2025, Bajraktarević won the Eredivisie title in his debut season with the Dutch giants. A pacey, left-footed right winger with sharp movement and a keen eye for goal, he is Bosnia's most exciting young attacker and his performances have already attracted Premier League interest. The 2026 World Cup could be his global breakthrough moment.
strengths: Pace and directness on the right wing
Winning mentality — Eredivisie champion in debut season
Creative and goal-threatening from wide positions
weaknesses: Minimal Eredivisie appearances in debut campaign (joined January 2025)
Physical adaptation to elite European demands ongoing

ermedin-demirovic.name: Ermedin Demirović
ermedin-demirovic.profile: Bosnia's deadliest striker and focal point of the attack, Demirović had a sensational 2024-25 Bundesliga season with 15 goals in 34 appearances, cementing his status as one of the Bundesliga's most lethal forwards. A powerful, direct centre-forward with intelligent movement and a clinical finishing instinct, he is the player opponents fear most and will be Bosnia's greatest threat at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Clinical finishing and elite goal-scoring instinct
Physical strength and aerial threat
Intelligent off-the-ball movement
weaknesses: Assist contributions are modest for a forward of his quality
Can be isolated if service is limited

jovo-lukic.name: Jovo Lukić
jovo-lukic.profile: A tall, left-footed forward who had a difficult spell at Universitatea Craiova in the first half of 2024-25 before making a career-defining move to Universitatea Cluj, where he became the Liga I top scorer in 2025-26. His physicality and aerial threat give Bosnia an alternative attacking option to Demirović, and his ability to hold up play makes him a useful squad weapon.
strengths: Aerial threat and physical presence up front
Left-footed technical quality
Strong link-up play as a target striker
weaknesses: Moderate goal return at Craiova in first half of 2024-25
Pace is below the elite level for a top forward

samed-bazdar.name: Samed Baždar
samed-bazdar.profile: A fast, direct winger who joined Spanish club Real Zaragoza from Partizan in July 2024, making 31 appearances and scoring 4 goals in the Segunda División, before being loaned to Jagiellonia Białystok in January 2026. Still only 21, Baždar's speed and directness give Bosnia a different attacking dimension — a runner who can exploit spaces in behind.
strengths: Explosive pace and directness
Ability to run in behind defensive lines
Young and improving at a high European level
weaknesses: Goal conversion rate still inconsistent
Final product (assists, goals) needs improvement

haris-tabakovic.name: Haris Tabaković
haris-tabakovic.profile: The most prolific Bosnian striker in recent domestic history, Tabaković scored 22 goals in 32 matches at Hertha BSC in 2023-24 before joining Hoffenheim for 2024-25 where he scored 6 goals in 22 appearances and was subsequently loaned to Borussia Mönchengladbach. A reliable penalty-box finisher, his intelligent movement and clinical touch make him Bosnia's most experienced domestic striker.
strengths: Lethal inside the penalty area
Consistent goal-scorer in the Bundesliga
Intelligent positioning and movement
weaknesses: Largely a penalty-box striker with limited contribution outside the area
Age means his best World Cup is likely 2026

edin-dzeko.name: Edin Džeko
edin-dzeko.profile: The greatest Bosnian footballer of all time, Džeko joined Schalke 04 in the 2. Bundesliga as a player-mentor and showed he can still score at the top with an impressive early-season return of 6 goals in 10 appearances. With over 100 Bosnia international goals and medals from Manchester City, Roma, Inter Milan and beyond, his mere presence transforms the team's mentality. At 39, his role is as much leadership and inspiration as it is goals.
strengths: Peerless experience and leadership
Clinical finishing still sharp in 2024-25
Hold-up play and link work remain elite
weaknesses: Age-related decline in pace and pressing
Cannot sustain a starting role across a full tournament

salah-zakaria.name: Salah Zakaria
salah-zakaria.profile: Salah Zakaria is Al-Duhail's first-choice goalkeeper and one of Qatar's most reliable shot-stoppers heading into 2026. A composed, technically sound keeper who commands his area well, he recorded 10 clean sheets in 22 league appearances during the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League season. At just 26, he represents the present and future of Qatari goalkeeping as the host nation plays their second-ever World Cup.
strengths: Strong shot-stopping reflexes
Clean sheet consistency (45% in 2024-25)
Command of penalty area
weaknesses: Limited exposure to elite European competition
Distribution under high pressure

meshaal-barsham.name: Meshaal Barsham
meshaal-barsham.profile: Meshaal Barsham is Al-Sadd's starting goalkeeper and a pivotal figure in the club's back-to-back Qatar Stars League title wins in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Named QSL Goalkeeper of the Season for 2024-25, Barsham is agile and highly capable of big saves in crucial moments. He will compete with Salah Zakaria for the starting berth at Qatar's 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Agility and quick reactions
Big-match temperament
Sweeper-keeper ability
weaknesses: 1.36 GA90 in rotated league appearances
Positioning on set pieces

mahmoud-abunada.name: Mahmoud Abunada
mahmoud-abunada.profile: Mahmoud Abunada is a 25-year-old goalkeeper who serves as Qatar's third-choice option heading into 2026. A tall and commanding presence at 1.91m, he plays for Al-Rayyan in the Qatar Stars League and is considered one of the country's brightest goalkeeping prospects. His inclusion in the World Cup squad reflects the depth of Qatari goalkeeping development.
strengths: Excellent reach and aerial dominance
Strong physique for high balls
Composed under pressure for his age
weaknesses: Limited senior international experience
Still developing shot-stopping consistency

boualem-khoukhi.name: Boualem Khoukhi
boualem-khoukhi.profile: Boualem Khoukhi is an Algerian-born Qatari centre-back who has been the defensive rock of both Al-Sadd and the national team for over a decade. A strong, experienced organiser at the back, he was part of Qatar's 2022 World Cup squad and brings invaluable experience to a host-nation group. Made 16 league appearances for Al-Sadd as they won the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League title.
strengths: Commanding in aerial duels
Positional intelligence and leadership
Experience in high-pressure international games
weaknesses: Pace against fast forwards is a concern at 34
Recovery speed in transitions

pedro-miguel.name: Pedro Miguel
pedro-miguel.profile: Pedro Miguel is a Portuguese-born Qatari left back who has been one of the most consistent defenders in the Qatar Stars League for years. Renowned for his technical ability, overlapping runs, and defensive solidity, he is a key part of Al-Sadd's title-winning backline. At 34, he provides experience and versatility as Qatar seeks to progress beyond the group stage.
strengths: Technical quality and composure on the ball
Accurate crossing from left back
Defensive positioning and reading of play
weaknesses: Pace limitations at his age against fast wingers
May struggle with elite opposition pressing high

sultan-al-brake.name: Sultan Al Brake
sultan-al-brake.profile: Sultan Al Brake is a versatile defender for Al-Duhail who can operate as a centre-back or right back, giving Qatar tactical flexibility. A Qatari international who was part of the 2022 World Cup squad on home soil, Al Brake brings domestic experience and solid defensive fundamentals to a young Qatari defensive unit.
strengths: Tactical versatility across defensive positions
Physicality in duels
Experience from Qatar 2022
weaknesses: Consistency levels can vary match to match
Aerial threat against taller forwards

al-hashmi-al-hussain.name: Al-Hashmi Al-Hussain
al-hashmi-al-hussain.profile: Al-Hashmi Al-Hussain is one of Qatar's most promising young defenders, having made his international debut in June 2024. The 22-year-old Al-Arabi centre-back is a tenacious tackler who is not afraid to be physical, and his elevation to the World Cup squad at this stage of his career underlines the faith placed in Qatar's next generation.
strengths: Aggressive in the tackle and strong in duels
Reading of opposition attacks
Potential for long international career
weaknesses: Still gaining top-level experience — can be caught in possession
Disciplinary record (3 yellow, 1 red in 11 appearances)

ayoub-al-alawi.name: Ayoub Al-Alawi
ayoub-al-alawi.profile: Ayoub Al-Alawi is Qatar's youngest outfield World Cup squad member at just 20 years old. The Al-Gharafa centre-back had limited league minutes in 2024-25, making just four appearances, but his physical attributes — standing at 187cm — make him a project player that coach Lopetegui wants exposed to World Cup football. He represents Qatar's generational investment in their defensive future.
strengths: Impressive height and physicality for his age
Strong aerially and good with his feet for a centre-back
High ceiling as a developing talent
weaknesses: Very limited senior club experience in 2024-25
Tactical and positional maturity still developing

issa-laye.name: Issa Laye
issa-laye.profile: Issa Laye is a tall, commanding centre-back who joined Al-Arabi on loan in January 2025. Standing at 188cm, he is a dominant aerial presence and fits Qatar's need for physical depth at centre-back. His no-nonsense defensive approach complements more technical defenders in the squad.
strengths: Dominant aerial presence at 188cm
Physical in ground duels
Good anticipation in the defensive line
weaknesses: Only half a season of Qatar Stars League experience in 2024-25
Limited involvement at the very top of the domestic game

lucas-mendes.name: Lucas Mendes
lucas-mendes.profile: Lucas Mendes is a Brazilian-born Qatari left-sided defender who has been a cornerstone of the Qatar national team for years. Now 35, the Al-Wakrah captain brings a wealth of experience and composure under pressure. He played 15 matches for Al-Wakrah in the 2024-25 season and remains a key organiser in the backline.
strengths: Experienced leader and organiser at the back
Strong positioning and game-reading
Aerial ability and physical durability
weaknesses: Age-related decline in pace could be exposed by fast attackers
Limited impact on attacking transitions

homam-al-amin.name: Homam Al-Amin
homam-al-amin.profile: Homam Al-Amin is the only Qatar 2026 squad member playing outside of Qatar, spending the 2024-25 season on loan at Cultural Leonesa in Spain's Primera Federación (third tier). The Al-Duhail-owned left back has developed his technical game in Spanish football, giving him a level of European exposure unique in the Qatar squad.
strengths: Technically polished from Spanish football development
Athleticism and work rate up and down the flank
Positional versatility as a left back or left wing-back
weaknesses: Playing in Spain's third division — gap to World Cup level is significant
Limited international caps relative to squad peers

ahmed-fathi.name: Ahmed Fathi
ahmed-fathi.profile: Ahmed Fathi is a combative and experienced defensive midfielder who has been a mainstay of the Qatar national team. A two-time Asian Cup winner (2019 and 2023), he specialises in breaking up play, winning second balls, and providing protection to the backline. His reading of the game and work ethic make him an effective base in Qatar's midfield.
strengths: Ball-winning and tackling in midfield
Positional discipline and defensive awareness
Asian Cup winning experience
weaknesses: Limited attacking output — rarely contributes goals or assists
Disciplinary record with yellow card accumulation

jassim-gaber.name: Jassim Gaber
jassim-gaber.profile: Jassim Gaber is a 23-year-old defensive midfielder or centre-back who provides versatile cover across Qatar's back third. Born in February 2002, he is one of the youngest midfielders in the squad and his inclusion reflects Qatar's long-term planning. After featuring for Al-Rayyan during the 2024-25 season, he brings energy and mobility to the holding role.
strengths: Energetic pressing and ball-winning ability
Versatility as a midfielder and defender
Young with high development potential
weaknesses: Still relatively inexperienced at senior level
Needs to develop passing range in possession phases

assim-madibo.name: Assim Madibo
assim-madibo.profile: Assim Madibo is Qatar's first-choice central defensive midfielder and the engine of the national team's midfield. Born in Sudan and naturalised Qatari, he is the primary ball-winner who sits in front of the back four and allows Abdulaziz Hatem to operate more freely. He was a standout figure during Qatar's Asian Cup title defences.
strengths: Elite ball-winning and pressing intensity
Physical presence in midfield duels
Leadership as Qatar's midfield anchor
weaknesses: Limited attack contribution — not a goal threat
Yellow card accumulation (5 in limited 2024-25 appearances)

abdulaziz-hatem.name: Abdulaziz Hatem
abdulaziz-hatem.profile: Abdulaziz Hatem is one of Qatar's most technically gifted midfielders, capable of dictating tempo and picking passes in tight spaces. Having played over 100 international caps, the Al-Rayyan veteran is the creative fulcrum of the national team's midfield alongside Madibo. Made 18 league appearances in 2024-25 and remains an important figure in Lopetegui's plans despite being 34.
strengths: Technical quality and passing range
Experience of 100+ international caps
Ability to control game tempo
weaknesses: Age-related drop in mobility and pressing output
Pace in transitions has diminished

karim-boudiaf.name: Karim Boudiaf
karim-boudiaf.profile: Karim Boudiaf is a deeply experienced box-to-box midfielder who has worn the Qatar national team shirt over 80 times. The Algerian-born Qatari international is known for his physicality, engine, and ability to contribute in both defensive and offensive phases. He was part of Qatar's 2022 World Cup squad and at 34 he provides tournament experience in the dressing room.
strengths: Box-to-box energy and stamina
Experience of major tournaments including 2022 World Cup
Strong in physical midfield battles
weaknesses: Declining mobility at 34
Tendency to accumulate yellow cards

mohammed-mannai.name: Mohammed Mannai
mohammed-mannai.profile: Mohammed Mannai is the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League Best Under-23 Player of the Season, making him one of the most exciting young talents in Qatari football. On loan at Al-Shamal from Al-Sadd, the 22-year-old defensive midfielder impressed throughout the campaign with energetic performances, earning his World Cup call-up on merit.
strengths: Award-winning form at U23 level in 2024-25
High energy and pressing intensity
Technical quality for a young defensive midfielder
weaknesses: Step up to World Cup intensity will be significant for a 22-year-old
Limited top-level experience compared to squad veterans

almoez-ali.name: Almoez Ali
almoez-ali.profile: Almoez Ali is Qatar's all-time leading scorer with 60 international goals in 126 appearances and the captain of Al-Duhail. He was the top scorer in Asia's 2026 World Cup qualifying with 12 goals, underlining his continued dominance at continental level. The Sudanese-born striker scored a record nine goals at the 2019 Asian Cup and is Qatar's most potent attacking threat entering 2026.
strengths: Elite finishing and movement in the box
Record-breaking international goal-scoring record
Ability to lead the line physically and technically
weaknesses: Effectiveness can depend on service quality from midfield
Inconsistency in club form across seasons

akram-afif.name: Akram Afif
akram-afif.profile: Akram Afif is Qatar's most celebrated footballer and a two-time AFC Player of the Year. The Al-Sadd left winger finished as joint-top scorer in the 2024-25 Qatar Stars League with 18 goals, driving Al-Sadd to back-to-back league titles. Afif has 127 international caps and 40 goals for Qatar, with his hat-trick of penalties in the 2024 Asian Cup final cementing his legendary status. He is the undisputed leader of Qatar's attack for 2026.
strengths: Lethal finishing and free-kick delivery
Dribbling ability and unpredictability in the final third
Unmatched big-game mentality — decisive in Asian Cup finals
weaknesses: Heavily relied upon — Qatar's attack can be one-dimensional without him
Physical intensity of World Cup tournament football over multiple games

tahsin-mohammed.name: Tahsin Mohammed
tahsin-mohammed.profile: Tahsin Mohammed is Qatar's most exciting teenage talent, born June 16, 2006, and one of the youngest players at the 2026 World Cup. The Al-Duhail winger is quick, direct, and blessed with natural technical ability. His inclusion in the 26-man squad at just 19 demonstrates the ambition of Qatar's footballing programme to fast-track gifted young players onto the world stage.
strengths: Electrifying pace and directness on the wing
Natural technical talent with outstanding potential
Fearless on-the-ball approach
weaknesses: Very young and inexperienced at professional level
Consistency and decision-making still developing

edmilson-junior.name: Edmilson Junior
edmilson-junior.profile: Edmilson Junior is a Brazilian-born Qatari international winger who plays on the right flank for Al-Duhail. A dynamic and technically skilled wide forward, he provides direct running, crosses, and goal threat from the right side, complementing Akram Afif on the other flank. His naturalisation for Qatar adds significant quality to the national team's wide attacking options.
strengths: Dynamic direct running and dribbling from the right
Technical quality and ability to create chances
International experience across multiple tournaments
weaknesses: Consistency of end product can fluctuate
Defensive tracking back is sometimes lacking

ahmed-al-janehi.name: Ahmed Al-Janehi
ahmed-al-janehi.profile: Ahmed Al-Janehi is a 24-year-old attacking midfielder or wide forward who had an impressive 2024-25 campaign for Al-Gharafa, registering 3 goals and 6 assists in the Qatar Stars League. His ability to operate between the lines and create for teammates as well as score gives Qatar a versatile option across the front line.
strengths: Creative vision and assist ability — 6 QSL assists in 2024-25
Technical quality in tight spaces
Versatility across attacking positions
weaknesses: Still developing his goal-scoring output
Can be inconsistent against physically dominant defenders

ahmed-alaa.name: Ahmed Alaa
ahmed-alaa.profile: Ahmed Alaa is a 32-year-old forward for Al-Rayyan who has been a consistent performer in the Qatar Stars League over many years. Known for his movement, link-up play, and eye for goal, he provides experienced attacking options for Qatar from the bench or wide positions. A reliable domestic campaigner, he brings consistency and experience to complement the squad's younger attackers.
strengths: Consistent performer across multiple QSL seasons
Intelligent movement and link-up play
Ability to operate across front line positions
weaknesses: Not an elite goal scorer by international standards
Pace may limit effectiveness against top-level defences

hassan-al-haydos.name: Hassan Al-Haydos
hassan-al-haydos.profile: Hassan Al-Haydos is Qatar's captain and most-capped player ever, with 188 international appearances and 41 goals. He came out of international retirement in June 2025 at the personal request of head coach Julen Lopetegui. A creative wide forward known for his dribbling, vision, and ability to perform in the biggest moments, Al-Haydos symbolises Qatari football.
strengths: Record-breaking international experience (188 caps)
Dribbling, vision, and quality in the final third
Leadership and motivational presence as captain
weaknesses: At 35, sustained high-intensity runs are limited
Physical output has declined from peak years

mohammed-muntari.name: Mohammed Muntari
mohammed-muntari.profile: Mohammed Muntari made history at the 2022 World Cup by scoring Qatar's only goal of the tournament — a memorable header against Senegal. Having joined Al-Gharafa on a free transfer in summer 2024, he scored 4 goals in 10 league appearances in his debut season. The 27-year-old provides a different physical profile up front compared to Almoez Ali, and his World Cup goal-scoring pedigree makes him a meaningful option.
strengths: Proven World Cup goalscorer
Strong and physical centre-forward play
Aerial ability and hold-up play
weaknesses: Limited appearances in 2024-25 — still settling at new club
Not the most prolific scorer at club level

yusuf-abdurisag.name: Yusuf Abdurisag
yusuf-abdurisag.profile: Yusuf Abdurisag is a 24-year-old winger who spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Al-Wakrah from parent club Al-Sadd. A pacey and energetic wide forward, he is one of Qatar's most dynamic young attackers with the ability to run in behind defences and create problems on the counter. His development loan at Al-Wakrah has given him valuable regular game time ahead of his first World Cup.
strengths: Pace and direct running in behind defences
Young age with high developmental ceiling
Ability to play across the front line
weaknesses: End product needs improvement — goals and assists not yet elite
Experience of high-pressure knockout football limited

marvin-keller.name: Marvin Keller
marvin-keller.profile: Marvin Keller is the long-serving Young Boys goalkeeper who has been the undisputed first choice in Bern for several seasons. A calm and technically sound shot-stopper, he earned his place as Switzerland's third-choice keeper through consistent Swiss Super League performances and UEFA Champions League experience. At the 2026 World Cup he serves as experienced domestic cover behind Kobel.
strengths: Shot-stopping reflexes
Command of the penalty area
Distribution with feet
weaknesses: Limited top-level European exposure
Tested by high-volume shot opponents

gregor-kobel.name: Gregor Kobel
gregor-kobel.profile: Gregor Kobel is Switzerland's undisputed number one and one of the top goalkeepers in the Bundesliga. After helping Dortmund reach the 2024 Champions League final and delivering another commanding season in 2024-25, Kobel arrives at the 2026 World Cup as one of the most reliable and dominant keepers in the tournament. His aerial presence, composure under pressure, and sweeping ability make him the cornerstone of Switzerland's compact defensive system.
strengths: Elite shot-stopping
Aerial dominance
Commanding presence in the box
weaknesses: Can be prone to distribution errors under intense pressure
Has not consistently reproduced peak UCL-level form in all Bundesliga matches

yvon-mvogo.name: Yvon Mvogo
yvon-mvogo.profile: Yvon Mvogo had arguably his best professional season in 2024-25, helping Lorient win the Ligue 2 title and earn promotion back to Ligue 1. A solid and experienced shot-stopper who has played across multiple European leagues, Mvogo provides reliable competition for the second-choice goalkeeper slot behind Kobel heading into the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Consistency at second-tier level
Experience across multiple European leagues
Solid reflexes on low shots
weaknesses: Limited top-flight exposure in recent seasons
Aerial command can be uncertain against physical strikers

manuel-akanji.name: Manuel Akanji
manuel-akanji.profile: Manuel Akanji is Switzerland's most accomplished center-back, joining Inter Milan on loan from Manchester City in 2024-25 and becoming a key figure in Simone Inzaghi's title-challenging side with 33 Serie A appearances. His ball-playing ability, aerial presence, and positional intelligence make him the defensive leader of the Swiss national team. He will be pivotal in marshalling Switzerland's back line through the knockout stages of the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Ball-playing from the back
Aerial dominance
Positional intelligence
weaknesses: Can be exposed by quick transitions against top pace
Occasionally rash in the challenge

aurele-amenda.name: Aurèle Amenda
aurele-amenda.profile: Aurèle Amenda is one of Switzerland's most exciting young defenders who moved to Eintracht Frankfurt in 2024 and earned limited but impactful Bundesliga minutes in his debut season (~200 minutes). A commanding center-back with excellent anticipation, strong dueling ability, and poise on the ball, Amenda represents the future of the Swiss defensive setup.
strengths: Strong in aerial and ground duels
Composure on the ball for his age
Positional anticipation
weaknesses: Limited Bundesliga minutes in 2024-25 (200 total)
Still building experience against top-level forwards

eray-comert.name: Eray Cömert
eray-comert.profile: Eray Cömert is a composed and technically capable center-back who has established himself in La Liga with Valencia. His 2024-25 season was disrupted by a hamstring injury that limited him to 16 La Liga appearances, but he combines solid defensive fundamentals with the technical quality prized in the Swiss national team and remains an important depth option.
strengths: Technical quality in possession
Intelligent reading of the game
Positional discipline
weaknesses: Injury susceptibility has limited availability
Aerial duels against elite strikers can be challenging

nico-elvedi.name: Nico Elvedi
nico-elvedi.profile: Nico Elvedi is a dependable and experienced center-back who has been a fixture for both Switzerland and Borussia Mönchengladbach for nearly a decade. Leading his club with 174 clearances in the 2024-25 Bundesliga, he has been a cornerstone of Switzerland's defensive solidity across multiple World Cups and European Championships. He brings calm leadership to the defensive unit.
strengths: Aerial dominance
High clearance volume and defensive organisation (174 in 2024-25)
Experience and consistency at the highest domestic level
weaknesses: Pace against quick forwards in behind
Ball progression from the back is functional rather than creative

luca-jaques.name: Luca Jäques
luca-jaques.profile: Luca Jäques is a promising young Swiss center-back who joined VfB Stuttgart on a permanent deal in February 2025 and quickly made an impression, capping his debut season by winning the DFB Pokal. A modern ball-playing defender who is composed under pressure and strong in one-on-one situations, Jäques is one of the most exciting young Swiss defenders heading into the World Cup.
strengths: Ball-playing from the back
Strong in one-on-one defending
Reading and anticipation
weaknesses: Still building Bundesliga experience with limited minutes in 2024-25
Tested by physical elite strikers at top-level

miro-muheim.name: Miro Muheim
miro-muheim.profile: Miro Muheim is a versatile and energetic left-back who has been a consistent performer for Hamburger SV, making 30 2. Bundesliga appearances in 2024-25. Known for his overlapping runs, defensive intensity, and ability to contribute to attacks from wide areas, Muheim has become a reliable option on the left flank for Switzerland.
strengths: Overlapping runs and attacking contribution from left-back
Defensive one-on-one ability
Work rate and pressing intensity
weaknesses: Crossing can be inconsistent under pressure
Transition defending when caught high up the pitch

ricardo-rodriguez.name: Ricardo Rodríguez
ricardo-rodriguez.profile: Ricardo Rodríguez is one of Switzerland's most experienced defenders, a veteran left-back who joined Real Betis on a free transfer in August 2024 after leaving Torino, making 18 La Liga appearances in 2024-25. Renowned for his delivery from set-pieces and dependable defensive performances, Rodríguez has been a fixture in Swiss squads for over a decade.
strengths: Set-piece delivery and crossing
Defensive positioning and veteran experience
Leadership within the defensive unit
weaknesses: Reduced pace at 32 against young attacking wingers
Limited to a depth role given squad age profile

silvan-widmer.name: Silvan Widmer
silvan-widmer.profile: Silvan Widmer is an experienced and versatile right-back who has served Switzerland well across multiple major tournaments. In 2024-25, his role at Mainz 05 shifted to a squad rotation option with only 3 starts across 27 Bundesliga appearances. His ability to play both full-back positions and deliver from set-pieces makes him valuable experienced depth for Switzerland.
strengths: Versatility across both full-back positions
Set-piece delivery and crossing
Experience across multiple major tournaments
weaknesses: Reduced to a rotational role at club level in 2024-25
Pace limitations against younger wingers

michel-aebischer.name: Michel Aebischer
michel-aebischer.profile: Michel Aebischer is a dynamic box-to-box midfielder who moved on loan from Bologna to Pisa for the 2024-25 Serie A season after years of consistent performances at Bologna during their historic Champions League qualification. A key figure in Switzerland's midfield for several years, he combines pressing intensity, ball recovery, and intelligent forward carrying.
strengths: Pressing intensity and ball recovery
Forward carrying from midfield
Intelligent off-the-ball movement
weaknesses: Pisa loan limited his profile compared to earlier Bologna seasons
Pass completion can drop under sustained high pressure

remo-freuler.name: Remo Freuler
remo-freuler.profile: Remo Freuler is one of Switzerland's most experienced and respected midfielders, a mainstay of the national team for nearly a decade. At Bologna in 2024-25, he made 28 Serie A appearances, recording 81 tackles across the season while contributing his trademark combination of elite pressing, defensive interceptions, and quality distribution. At 33, this may be his final World Cup.
strengths: Elite work rate and tackling volume across a full season
Intelligent pressing and interceptions
Experience as a tournament veteran for Switzerland
weaknesses: Aging legs may limit back-to-back high-intensity performances
Declining vertical passing range compared to peak years

ardon-jashari.name: Ardon Jashari
ardon-jashari.profile: Ardon Jashari was the breakout star of the 2024-25 Belgian Pro League season at Club Brugge, earning both Player of the Year and Young Player of the Year honours after a dominant campaign. A dynamic defensive and progressive midfielder with exceptional ball retention, dribbling under pressure, and line-breaking passing ability, his move to AC Milan in summer 2025 cemented his status as one of Europe's most exciting young midfield talents.
strengths: Ball retention and dribbling under pressure
Progressive line-breaking passing
Defensive intensity and one-on-one ball recovery
weaknesses: Yet to be tested consistently at Serie A level after summer 2025 move
Can overcommit in pressing situations

fabian-rieder.name: Fabian Rieder
fabian-rieder.profile: Fabian Rieder is a versatile and technically gifted attacking midfielder who spent the 2024-25 season on loan at VfB Stuttgart from Stade Rennais, contributing 8 assists and 1 goal in 21 Bundesliga appearances and winning the DFB Pokal. A player with an excellent eye for the through-ball and solid pressing intelligence, Rieder subsequently made a permanent move to FC Augsburg.
strengths: Creative passing and through-ball delivery
Pressing intelligence
Versatility across midfield and attacking positions
weaknesses: Inconsistency in high-pressure moments
Defensive contribution still developing at the highest level

djibril-sow.name: Djibril Sow
djibril-sow.profile: Djibril Sow is a powerful and progressive defensive midfielder who has established himself as a key player at Sevilla after his move from Eintracht Frankfurt. With a 90% pass completion rate and strong defensive metrics across 30 La Liga appearances in 2024-25, Sow provides both disciplined protection and quality ball circulation. He is the athletic engine in the Swiss midfield.
strengths: High pass completion rate (90% in La Liga)
Powerful ball-carrying and progression
Defensive tackling and recovery actions
weaknesses: Goal contribution from midfield remains modest
Can occasionally overdo risky carries into pressure

granit-xhaka.name: Granit Xhaka
granit-xhaka.profile: Granit Xhaka is the heartbeat of the Swiss national team and one of the most transformed midfielders in European football. His 2024-25 season with Bayer Leverkusen — where he led the Bundesliga in line-breaking passes (550) and helped win the domestic double — was arguably the peak of his career renaissance. Now captaining Sunderland in the Premier League, Xhaka brings unparalleled leadership, vision, and passing range to Switzerland.
strengths: Elite line-breaking passing range — led Bundesliga in 2024-25
Leadership and on-pitch decision-making
High defensive duel contribution and coverage
weaknesses: Occasional disciplinary issues under sustained pressure
Reduced burst of pace at 33

denis-zakaria.name: Denis Zakaria
denis-zakaria.profile: Denis Zakaria enjoyed one of the best seasons of his career at Monaco in 2024-25, scoring 6 goals and providing 5 assists from central midfield while helping Monaco qualify for the Champions League. Setting personal career bests in goals, assists, and tackles with 33 appearances, Zakaria re-established himself as a top-level player after years of injury disruption.
strengths: Powerful surging runs from deep midfield
Goal and assist contribution from central areas
Defensive intensity and tackling volume
weaknesses: Injury history has disrupted consistency throughout his career
Can be tactically undisciplined when pressing aggressively

ruben-vargas.name: Ruben Vargas
ruben-vargas.profile: Ruben Vargas is a versatile and direct winger who split the 2024-25 season between FC Augsburg in the Bundesliga (August–January) and Sevilla in La Liga after a January 2025 transfer. Known for his direct running, intelligent movement off the ball, and ability to cut inside, Vargas is a key creative and attacking threat on the left flank for Switzerland.
strengths: Direct dribbling and one-on-one ability
Intelligent movement to create space
Contributes in both attack and pressing phases
weaknesses: End product in front of goal can be inconsistent
Winter transfer disrupted early-season rhythm at Augsburg

zeki-amdouni.name: Zeki Amdouni
zeki-amdouni.profile: Zeki Amdouni spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Benfica in the Primeira Liga, where he scored 5 goals in 18 appearances while developing his game in a top Portuguese club environment. A powerful and intelligent centre-forward with excellent link-up play and movement in behind defensive lines, Amdouni is one of Switzerland's most technically rounded attackers.
strengths: Movement in behind defensive lines
Physical presence and hold-up play in attack
Link-up ability and combination play
weaknesses: Shot accuracy at Benfica was below expectations (7 on target from 29 shots)
Adapting between different club environments has disrupted rhythm

breel-embolo.name: Breel Embolo
breel-embolo.profile: Breel Embolo had his finest season in years at Monaco in 2024-25, scoring 7 goals and providing 7 assists in 39 appearances — setting career highs across multiple attacking and defensive metrics. The powerful and versatile forward combines exceptional physicality with sharp pressing intelligence and clever movement. Now at Rennes, Embolo remains Switzerland's most complete and experienced attacking option entering the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Physical power and hold-up play
Pressing intensity from the front
Goal and assist contributions from varied positions
weaknesses: Injury proneness has been a recurring concern throughout his career
Can go quiet in matches when service from midfield is limited

dan-ndoye.name: Dan Ndoye
dan-ndoye.profile: Dan Ndoye had a breakthrough 2024-25 Serie A season at Bologna, scoring 8 goals and providing 4 assists in 30 appearances, including the winning goal in the Coppa Italia final — Bologna's first major trophy in over 50 years. An electric winger whose ball-carrying statistics were bettered by only five players in all of Serie A, his versatility, pace, and ability to perform in big matches make him one of the most dangerous wide players at the 2026 World Cup.
strengths: Electric ball-carrying and dribbling — Serie A top 5
Versatility across both wings and attacking positions
Proven big-game delivery at the highest level
weaknesses: Shot accuracy on high volume can be inconsistent
Decision-making in the final third under sustained defensive pressure

noah-okafor.name: Noah Okafor
noah-okafor.profile: Noah Okafor had a difficult 2024-25 season, making only 11 Serie A appearances for AC Milan before a planned RB Leipzig loan fell through following a failed medical, then moving on loan to Napoli in February 2025 where he contributed sparingly but won the Scudetto. A player of exceptional pace, technical quality, and positional versatility, he remains one of the highest-ceiling players in the Swiss squad. His move to Leeds for 2025-26 provides a new platform.
strengths: Explosive pace and directness
Technical quality in tight spaces
Versatility across all forward positions
weaknesses: Club inconsistency throughout 2024-25 limited form and confidence
Final ball and penalty area decision-making need sharpening

christian-fassnacht.name: Christian Fassnacht
christian-fassnacht.profile: Christian Fassnacht returned to Young Boys in January 2025 after a stint at Norwich City, and immediately reverted to the prolific form that made him one of the Swiss Super League's most feared forwards, scoring 11 goals in just 18 league appearances in the second half of the season. His clinical instinct, intelligent movement, and technical ability remain fully intact at 31.
strengths: Clinical finishing at Swiss Super League level (11 goals in 18 apps)
Intelligent off-the-ball movement
Experience and leadership as a senior forward in the squad
weaknesses: Period at Norwich City saw limited minutes and disrupted form
Pace naturally declining with age at 31

cedric-itten.name: Cédric Itten
cedric-itten.profile: Cédric Itten is a powerful and direct centre-forward who had a productive 2024-25 season at Young Boys, scoring 8 goals in 34 Swiss Super League appearances before earning a move to Fortuna Düsseldorf in the 2. Bundesliga. A traditional number nine with physical strength, aerial presence, and an ability to hold up play, Itten provides a different attacking profile to the other Swiss forwards.
strengths: Physical hold-up play and link-up with runners
Aerial threat from crosses and set-pieces
Work rate and pressing from the front line
weaknesses: Swiss Super League background limits exposure to elite-level defenders
Finishing can be streaky over a full season

johan-manzambi.name: Johan Manzambi
johan-manzambi.profile: Johan Manzambi is one of the most exciting young Swiss forwards to emerge in recent seasons, breaking onto the Bundesliga scene at SC Freiburg in the second half of 2024-25 with 2 goals and an assist across six successive appearances. A quick, direct, and technically gifted winger, his form earned him his first senior Switzerland call-ups and a place in the 2026 World Cup squad at just 22.
strengths: Explosive direct running and dribbling at pace
Technical quality under pressure
Hunger and confidence of a young talent with rising trajectory
weaknesses: Very limited top-flight Bundesliga experience (11 appearances in 2024-25)
Decision-making under defensive pressure still developing
